nodes.title: Isavasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sees the moving world as pervaded by the Lord; places action, renunciation, knowledge and immortality together.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kena Upanishad
nodes.summary: Asks what directs mind, speech and senses; the Yaksha encounter exposes the gods' dependence on Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Katha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Nachiketas questions Death about the self, the good and the pleasant, immortality, and disciplined knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.summary: Modern commentary by Swami Nirmalananda Giri. Interpretations and additional anecdotes are distinct from the preceding Upanishad translation.

nodes.title: Prasna Upanishad
nodes.summary: Six seekers question Pippalada on origins, life-breath, sleep, Om and the sixteen-part Purusha.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mundaka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Angiras answers Saunaka's question about knowing all; distinguishes higher and lower knowledge and teaches Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mandukya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets Om through waking, dream, deep sleep and the fourth, nondual self; followed by Gaudapada's Karika.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Taittiriya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Combines student instruction with layered accounts of self and bliss; Bhrigu investigates Brahman through austerity.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.summary: Modern commentary by Swami Nirmalananda Giri. Interpretations and additional anecdotes are distinct from the preceding Upanishad translation.

nodes.title: Aitareya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narrates the Self's creation and entry into embodied life, then identifies consciousness with Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Aitareya Upanishad — Nirmalananda Giri commentary
nodes.summary: Modern commentary by Swami Nirmalananda Giri. Interpretations and additional anecdotes are distinct from the preceding Upanishad translation.

evidence.quote: Commentary on the Aitereya Upanishad–by Swami Nirmalananda Giri

nodes.title: Chandogya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Links chant, Om, breath and cosmic correspondences to dialogues on Brahman, the self, and the infinite.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Chandogya Upanishad — Nirmalananda Giri commentary
nodes.summary: Modern commentary by Swami Nirmalananda Giri. Interpretations and additional anecdotes are distinct from the preceding Upanishad translation.

evidence.quote: Commentary on the Chandogya Upanishad–by Swami Nirmalananda Giri

nodes.title: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses ritual symbolism and dialogues involving Yajnavalkya, Maitreyi, Gargi and Janaka to investigate the self and Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Brahma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Pippalada teaches Saunaka about the inner Brahman, life-breath and the sacred thread understood as knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kaivalya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma teaches Asvalayana that faith, devotion, meditation and renunciation lead to the highest knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya explains Avimukta and renunciation; treats the conditions and conduct of the wandering ascetic.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Svetasvatara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Investigates the cause of existence, the Lord, the self, nature and the discipline through which reality is known.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Hamsa Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sanatkumara teaches Gautama the Hamsa discipline, breath-linked contemplation and inner sound.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Aruni Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma instructs Aruni on abandoning ritual possessions and worldly ties for the knowledge of Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Garbha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents a traditional account of embryonic development, bodily elements and the body interpreted as sacrifice.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Narayana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Praises Narayana as the source and identity of all; expounds the eight-syllable Om Namo Narayanaya mantra.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Paramahamsa Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma answers Narada about the inward freedom, duties and outward simplicity of the Paramahamsa ascetic.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Amrita Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains how desire binds the mind and how the mind freed from sense objects becomes a means of liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Amrita-Nada Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses the chariot of Om as an image for contemplation and sets out disciplines of yoga and breath.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atharvasiras Upanishad
nodes.summary: Identifies Rudra with the gods, cosmic regions and Om; explains the one principle through many divine names.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atharvasikha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Atharva answers sages about meditation on Om and its four aspects, deities and Vedic correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maitrayani Upanishad
nodes.summary: King Brihadratha renounces his throne and asks the sage Sakayana for self-knowledge beyond decaying embodiment.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kaushitaki Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contains dialogues about rebirth, life-breath and consciousness, including Indra-Pratardana and Balaki-Ajatasatru.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Brihad Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Busunda questions Kalagni Rudra about sacred ash, Rudraksha and Shaiva observance as a path to liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nrisimhatapini Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents Poorva and Uttara Narasimha Tapaniya translations on Narasimha, mantra, Om and the supreme self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kalagni Rudra Upanishad
nodes.summary: Kalagnirudra explains the three ash marks of Tripundra and their ritual and contemplative correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maitreya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Retells Brihadratha's disenchantment with embodied life and sets out self-knowledge and the renunciant's discipline.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Subala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes cosmic emergence and dissolution, the inner self and Narayana as the basis of beings.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kshurika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses a sharp knife of wisdom and inward yoga as imagery for cutting attachment; this version marks verses 2–9 unavailable.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mantrika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents the subtle, imperishable reality through swan imagery and the relation of knowledge, nature and the absolute.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sarva Sara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Defines bondage, liberation, ignorance, knowledge, consciousness states, sheaths, individual self and the absolute.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Niralamba Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses a sequence of questions and answers to define Brahman, God, the individual, nature, knowledge and liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Suka Rahasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Shiva teaches Suka the inner meaning of great Upanishadic sayings, including That Thou Art.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Vajrasuchika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Examines what makes a Brahmana and rejects body, birth and mere social designation as sufficient criteria.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tejo-Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches meditation on the seed of spiritual light and develops knowledge of the nondual self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nada Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets Om as a bird and develops contemplation on inner sound as a means of freeing the mind.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Dhyana-Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Connects seed-syllable, spiritual sound, contemplation and yogic processes with the supreme state beyond sound.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Brahma Vidya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains Om through its syllables, their Vedic and divine correspondences, inner location and dissolution.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga Tattva Upanishad
nodes.summary: Vishnu teaches Brahma the relation of yoga and knowledge and describes yogic disciplines leading to liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atma-Bodha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contemplates Narayana and Om as inner Brahman and develops assertions of the self's freedom and consciousness.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Narada Parivrajaka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narada asks Brahma about renunciation; treats eligibility, conduct, classifications and inner knowledge of ascetics.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Trisikhi Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: A Brahmana questions the Sun about body, self and cause; the reply links cosmology, inner faculties and yoga.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sita Upanishad
nodes.summary: Prajapati explains Sita as primordial nature and divine power, relating her to sound, knowledge and manifestation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga Chudamani Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches breath, Hamsa and yogic ascent; this supplied translation explicitly omits verses 2–29.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nirvana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes the Paramahamsa through inward renunciation and symbolic identifications of the ascetic life.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mandala Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: The solar Narayana teaches Yajnavalkya eightfold yoga, knowledge and inward contemplation of light.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Dakshinamurti Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sages ask Markandeya about his enduring life and joy; he teaches the secret knowledge and mantra of Dakshinamurti.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sarabha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Praises Shiva as supreme and narrates Sarabha's subduing of Narasimha within this text's Shaiva presentation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Skanda Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents the identity of Shiva and Vishnu and teaches the nonseparation of the individual self and the divine.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tripadvibhuti Mahanarayana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents Narayana as the source of all beings and cosmic forces; expounds Om Namo Narayanaya through eight-syllable mantra and inward realization.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Advaya Taraka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches nondual reality through neti-neti, inner light, Taraka yoga and guidance by a qualified teacher.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rama Rahasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Hanuman explains Rama's sacred formulae, their ritual arrangements and their liberating significance.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rama Tapaniya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contains Poorva and Uttara parts on Rama, Sita, devotional visualization and the saving Rama mantra.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Vasudeva Upanishad
nodes.summary: Vasudeva teaches Narada the rules and significance of the upward Vaishnava forehead mark.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mudgala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets the Purusha Sukta in terms of Vishnu's pervasion, the fourfold Purusha and liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sandilya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Atharvan answers Sandilya on eightfold yoga, including ethical disciplines, postures, breath and meditation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Paingala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya teaches Paingala about secondless Brahman, creation, inner faculties and liberating knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Bhikshuka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Classifies four forms of mendicant ascetic and describes their differing modes of life.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Begins with Narayana and creation, then develops teachings about mind, detachment and liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sariraka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes bodily elements, sense and action organs, inner faculties, qualities and related correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga Sikha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sets out yoga centered on Om, concentration and the relation of yogic realization to knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Turiyatita Avadhuta Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narayana explains the rare Avadhuta who has passed beyond ordinary distinctions and lives in the supreme self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sannyasa Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes the transition to renunciation, including rites, qualifications and conduct of the ascetic.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Paramahamsa-Parivrajaka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narayana answers Brahma about qualifications and conduct of the Paramahamsa wandering monk.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Aksha Malika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Guha answers Prajapati about the materials, construction, consecration and use of a rosary.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Avyakta Upanishad
nodes.summary: This supplied item presents transliterated Nasadiya, Hiranyagarbha and Purusha Suktas under stages of cosmic emergence.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Ekakshara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Praises the one imperishable reality as the source, indweller and sustainer of the world.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Annapurna Upanishad
nodes.summary: Ribhu instructs Nidagha on self-knowledge, mental freedom and liberation, in a teaching connected with Annapurna.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Surya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Identifies the Sun with the world-self, Brahman and the sources of gods, elements, Vedas and life.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Akshi Upanishad
nodes.summary: Samkriti praises the Sun and receives teachings on knowledge and yoga beyond ordinary embodiment.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Adhyatma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains superimposition of body and possessions on the self and teaches discrimination and realization of Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kundika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes the stages and inward requirements of renunciation after studentship and household life.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Savitri Upanishad
nodes.summary: Pairs Savitar and Savitri across cosmic and human correspondences and expounds the Savitri formula.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Distinguishes the bodily self, inner self and supreme self in an account attributed to Angiras.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Pasupata Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes Pasupati as the power behind mind and senses and as the self-shining witness of beings.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Para-Brahma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Pippalada teaches Saunaka about Brahman, creation and the inward significance of the sacred thread.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Avadhuta Upanishad
nodes.summary: Dattatreya explains to Samkriti the Avadhuta's freedom from worldly bonds and conventions.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tripura Tapini Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents Tripura as divine power and supreme reality and expounds her mantra through Vedic correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Devi Upanishad
nodes.summary: The Goddess answers the gods by declaring herself Brahman, nature, consciousness and the forms of the universe.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tripura Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses symbolic verse to describe the Goddess Tripura, her abodes, powers and mantra.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Katharudra Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma answers the gods with instructions on renunciation and knowledge of the supreme self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Bhavana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Maps the body and its constituents onto the Sri Chakra and the inward worship of divine power.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rudra Hridaya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Vyasa answers Suka by teaching the unity of Rudra, Vishnu, Uma and the other divine forms.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga-Kundalini Upanishad
nodes.summary: Relates control of mental impressions and life-breath to diet, posture and Kundalini-oriented yoga.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Bhasma Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Shiva teaches Bhusunda the preparation, application and sacred significance of ash.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rudraksha Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Kalagnirudra tells Bhusunda the origin of Rudraksha beads from his tears and their traditional uses.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Ganapati Upanishad
nodes.summary: Addresses Ganapati as the manifest principle and Brahman, with praise, mantra and a meditation form.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Jabala Darsana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Dattatreya teaches Samkriti the eight branches of yoga and their ethical and bodily disciplines.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tara Sara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya answers Brihaspati about Avimukta and the saving significance of sacred formulae.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maha Vakya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma explains inward realization through Hamsa-Soham, breath control and contemplation of the solar Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Pancha Brahma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains five aspects of Shiva through cosmic, ritual, Vedic and bodily correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Pranagnihotra Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets eating and the life-breaths as an inward sacrifice, with the body as a sacrificial field.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Gopala-Tapaniya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma answers sages about Krishna as supreme reality, with the Gopala mantra and devotional contemplation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Krishna Upanishad
nodes.summary: Connects Rama's forest sages with Krishna's Gopis and interprets Krishna's companions as personified qualities.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yajnavalkya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya teaches Janaka about the transition into renunciation and the conduct of the monk.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Varaha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Varaha teaches Ribhu about reality, bodily principles, self-knowledge and yogic discipline.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Satyayaniya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Treats the mind as the cause of bondage or liberation and develops renunciation and devotion toward Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Hayagriva Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma teaches Narada mantras of horse-headed Hayagriva as lord of knowledge and Vedic learning.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Dattatreya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narayana teaches Brahma contemplation and mantra of Dattatreya as the infinite Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Garuda Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents a traditional Garuda-associated mantra transmission for protection against poison.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kali Santarana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma gives Narada the sixteen-name Hare Rama and Hare Krishna formula as the means of crossing Kali.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Jabali Upanishad
nodes.summary: Jabali answers Pippalada about the being, Pasupati, bondage and liberation through knowledge and sacred ash.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Saubhagya Lakshmi Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narayana teaches the gods the knowledge and worship of Sri, followed by yogic instruction.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sarasvati-Rahasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Asvalayana explains praise and contemplation of Sarasvati and develops knowledge of the supreme self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Bahvricha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Declares the Goddess the original reality from whom the gods and the universe arise, and identifies her with consciousness.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Muktika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Rama teaches Hanuman a 108-Upanishad curriculum, Vedic affiliations, liberation and the dissolution of mental impressions.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Gaudapada’s Mandukya Karika
nodes.summary: Four chapters of metrical philosophical exposition follow the twelve verses of the Mandukya; the Karika is a separate composition.

nodes.title: Nrisimha Poorva Tapaniya
nodes.summary: First of the two Narasimha Tapaniya translations supplied under catalog item 27.

nodes.title: Nrisimha Uttara Tapaniya
nodes.summary: Second Narasimha Tapaniya translation; includes Om, the four consciousness aspects and the supreme self.

nodes.title: Rama Poorva Tapaniya
nodes.summary: First part of the Rama Tapaniya item, with mantra and devotional visualization.

nodes.title: Rama Uttara Tapaniya
nodes.summary: Second part, including Shiva’s Rama mantra and repeated identification of Rama with supreme reality.

nodes.title: Nachiketas and Death
nodes.summary: Nachiketas refuses transient rewards and asks Death to resolve what remains after a person dies. Death teaches self-knowledge and immortality.

nodes.title: The chariot of the self
nodes.summary: The self is the rider, body the chariot, intellect the charioteer, mind the reins and senses the horses; disciplined discrimination directs the journey.

evidence.quote: 1-III-3. Know the Self to be the master of the chariot, and the body to be the chariot. Know the intellect

nodes.title: The good and the pleasant
nodes.summary: Death distinguishes the good from the pleasant and commends Nachiketas for choosing lasting understanding.

evidence.quote: serving different purposes, blind man. Good accrues to him who, of these two, chooses the preferable.

nodes.title: The Yaksha, the gods and Uma
nodes.summary: Agni and Vayu fail to master a mysterious Yaksha. Uma explains to Indra that their victory depended on Brahman.

evidence.quote: and appeared before them, but they knew not who this Yaksha (worshipful Being) was.

nodes.title: Six seekers question Pippalada
nodes.summary: Six students approach Pippalada, live a year in discipline, then ask about origins, life-breath, sleep, Om and the sixteenfold person.

notes: All 108 numbered Muktika catalog entries were found in the supplied compilation. Catalog numbers are navigation identifiers, not composition dates.

PDF page numbers are one-based physical pages, not printed page numbers. Ten modern commentaries sometimes begin on the same PDF page as the end of the translation; both nodes therefore legitimately share a boundary page.
The Mandukya translation proper occupies pages 181–182; Gaudapada’s separately titled Karika occupies pages 182–193, followed by Nirmalananda Giri’s modern commentary on pages 193–197.

Nrisimhatapini is catalog item 27; the compilation supplies separate Poorva and Uttara translations and explicitly notes the alternate counting. They are child sections, not two extra entries in the 108.
Rama Tapaniya also contains Poorva and Uttara sections; both remain children of the one catalog entry.
Kshurika explicitly marks verses 2–9 unavailable; Yoga Chudamani marks verses 2–29 unavailable. These gaps belong to the supplied edition and are not silently filled.
Avyakta as supplied presents transliterated Nasadiya, Hiranyagarbha and Purusha Suktas with a compiler-style introduction; it is indexed as supplied, without asserting textual-critical completeness.
All summaries and episodes refer to the supplied translations. Extra anecdotes and interpretations inside modern commentaries are not labeled as original Upanishadic stories.
Vedic affiliations, where recorded, follow the compilation’s traditional colophons and Muktika grouping; affiliation is not proof that the supplied independent Samhita PDF contains that Upanishad.
Thematic comparisons are editorial navigation links. They do not establish chronology, textual derivation or uniform doctrine. Sectarian differences are retained.

Tags record terms attested in the primary translation, including recurring invocations; they are discovery aids rather than proof of an episode-level or doctrinal relationship. Curated edges carry their own passage evidence.
